record.context_brief: MDM for a circle (horseshoe conjecture range)
record.original_question: Fix r > 0. A maximal distance minimizer (also called an r-minimizer) for a compact set M \subset \mathbb{R}^d is a connected compact set \Sigma of minimal length (one-dimensional Hausdorff measure H^1(\Sigma)) among connected compact sets satisfying M \subset B_r(\Sigma), where B_r(\Sigma) is the closed r-neighborhood of \Sigma. For the planar case where M is a circle of radius R > r, determine the structure of a maximal distance minimizer for M (equivalently, decide what the minimizers are) in the parameter range r < R < 4.98r.

evidence.quote:
For a given compact set M ⊂ Rd and a given positive number r > 0, consider the problem of finding a connected compact
set Σ of minimal length (one-dimensional Hausdorff measure H1 ) such that

                                M ⊂ Br (Σ),

where Br (Σ) denotes the closed r-neighborhood of the set Σ. We refer to such a set Σ as a Maximal distance minimizer
(MDM or r-minimizer).

Question 1.1. What is a maximal distance minimizer for M = ∂BR with R > r? The problem remains open for 4.98r >
R > r.

Miranda, Paolini and Stepanov conjectured in [22] that any minimizer for a circle of radius R > r is a horseshoe id est
a union of an arc of a circle of radius R − r and two segments of its tangent lines.
   The conjecture is confirmed in [7] for R > 4.98r. For smaller values of 4.98r > R > r the hypothesis remains unproven.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let r > 0 and let M ⊂ ℝ² be a compact set. For a closed set Σ ⊂ ℝ², write B_r(Σ) = { x ∈ ℝ² : dist(x, Σ) ≤ r } for the closed r-neighborhood of Σ. A maximal distance minimizer (or r-minimizer) for M is a connected compact set Σ ⊂ ℝ² that minimizes the one-dimensional Hausdorff measure H¹(Σ) among all connected compact sets satisfying M ⊂ B_r(Σ).

Take M = ∂B_R(0) to be the circle of radius R > r centered at the origin. A "horseshoe" is, by definition, the union of an arc of a circle of radius R − r concentric with M together with two line segments tangent to that arc at its endpoints, of lengths chosen so that the r-neighborhood of this union covers M.

Problem. For every R in the range r < R < 4.98 r, determine the structure of every maximal distance minimizer Σ for M = ∂B_R(0). In particular, decide whether every such minimizer must be a horseshoe.
artifact.status_search_result: The horseshoe conjecture of Miranda–Paolini–Stepanov has been confirmed for circles of radius R > 4.98 r (Cherkashin–Teplitskaya, arXiv:1511.01026, ESAIM:COCV 2018), but for the remaining range r < R < 4.98 r the conjecture is still unproven and is listed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: On the horseshoe conjecture for maximal distance minimizers
status_evidence.snippet: The conjecture of Miranda, Paolini and Stepanov about the set of minimizers for M a circumference of radius R>0 has been proved for the case when r < R/4.98.
status_evidence.claim: The horseshoe conjecture is established only for R > 4.98 r.

status_evidence.snippet: Conjecture confirmed for R > 4.98 r; for smaller values 4.98 r > R > r the hypothesis remains unproven.
